Summary and assessment adjusted using Financial Stability Report insights:
- The intermeeting 50 bp cut, lower IOER, expanded T-bill purchases, and extended term/overnight repos are a classic countercyclical response aimed at maintaining ample reserves and preventing money market stress. The lower primary credit rate adds a backstop to bank funding.
- The FSR highlighted elevated valuation pressures and high business leverage heading into 2020, as well as vulnerabilities in short-term funding markets and nonbank intermediation—illustrated by the September 2019 repo stresses. These factors could amplify the adverse effects of the coronavirus shock on activity and credit.
- Offsetting these vulnerabilities, the FSR also emphasized strong bank capital and liquidity, and post-crisis reforms that reduce run risk at core institutions. The Fed’s chosen implementation tools directly target the funding-risk channel the FSR flagged, supporting policy transmission by lowering external finance premia. With inflation pressures muted and expectations anchored, easing is consistent with price stability.
- Net tone: still negative due to the emergency nature of the action and “evolving risks,” but buffered by targeted liquidity operations and solid bank resilience.
